dialog.body: Public Works storm line, this is Kevin.
Good afternoon, Kevin. My name is Luz Ortiz. I understand this is the storm line, and I know it's Saturday and City Hall is closed, so I appreciate that somebody picks up.
Yep, we keep this one going on weekends after a storm. What's going on?

Well, I wrote it all down so I don't skip anything. Hold on, let me get my glasses. Okay. This is about the water on the street after the soaker that ended Thursday, two days ago. The water is over the curb and across the whole sidewalk. It's been sitting there since Wednesday night.
Two days later and it's still there? Okay, I'm writing that down. Over the curb, across the sidewalk.
Yes. And this morning a delivery truck, a big box truck, tried to pull through it and got stuck. The driver had to wait for a tow. He was blocking half the road for almost an hour.
Oof. Was anybody hurt?

No, nobody was hurt. He was just angry, and I don't blame him. I was watching from my window. The thing is, this is not new. I have called before about this same spot, and I was told it was a state road. So it wasn't the city's responsibility. That was the whole answer I got.
Right, okay. Do you remember who you talked to, or roughly when?
I don't have a name written down. It was some time ago. I only wrote down that they said state road, and then nothing happened. So here we are again, with a truck in the water.

Understood. And I'm not going to just repeat that to you. Some of those roads are state-maintained, but the drains and the catch basins along them can still be a different story, so it's worth having somebody look. Can you tell me where this is? Cross street, address, whatever you've got.

I would rather not give my address on this call. I can describe the location. It's on the main road, near the corner where the road dips, a few car lengths before the light. You can see where the water collects. It's the low point.
Okay. Without a street name that's tough for a crew to find, though. Is there a landmark you can give me?

Hmm. Let me think how to say this. It's a couple of blocks from Spring Street. There's a coffee shop on Spring Street where I sit and do my paperwork, my bills and my letters, and I walk down from there. It's the stretch right below it, going toward the water.
Okay, below Spring Street, heading toward the harbor, at the low spot before the light. That helps some. I'll put all that in the notes.

Thank you. Now, what I really want to know is who I call to get it checked. Because I've been told state, and I don't know who is the state. Is there a number? Who do I call so this doesn't just get passed along again?

Fair question. So here's how I'd do it. I'll log it with us as a drain and flooding report, and I'll flag it for the supervisor so they can figure out whether it's ours or the state's. If it turns out to be the state highway department's, our folks can pass it to them directly. You shouldn't have to chase it yourself.

I would appreciate that. Because the last time, I was simply told it wasn't the city's, and I hung up with nothing. That is a long time to have water on a sidewalk. People with strollers are walking out into the road.
Yeah, that's a real problem, I get it. Is the water moving at all, or is it just sitting there? Any drain you can see, leaves piled on it?
I wrote that down too. There is a grate near the curb, and it looks covered with leaves and some trash. The water does not go down it. It just sits.

Okay, so possibly a blocked grate. Covered in leaves, water not draining. That's useful. Let me read it back. Water over the curb and across the sidewalk since Wednesday night, truck stuck this morning, previous report said state road, grate looks blocked. Below Spring Street near the low spot before the light. Did I get it?
Yes, that's right. Exactly right.
Good. Can I get a callback number in case the supervisor has questions?
Yes. It's four zero one, five five five, zero one seven two.
Four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-seven-two. And it's Luz Ortiz, right?
Yes, Luz, L-U-Z, Ortiz.
Got it. I can't promise a time, since crews are stretched after a storm like this, but this goes on the list for Monday at the latest, and sooner if the supervisor sees it today.
Monday is a long way off with that truck situation, but I understand. Please make sure it says the water has been there two days. I don't want it treated like it just happened.
I'll put that in bold. Two days standing water, truck got stuck.
Thank you, Kevin. I'll be waiting for the call.
You got it, Ms. Ortiz. Take care, and stay out of that puddle.
